android.desc:
Break the loop. Don't scroll – discover.
Bliip is not another social media app. It's a pocket-sized radar for your sector and a tool for documenting everyday life.

Tired of algorithms deciding for you? Do you feel the digital world has become unbearably staged and artificial? We built Bliip to break free from this trap. It's a network built on absolute honesty and reciprocity. We collect only fleeting, real moments here – no censorship, no artificial enhancements.

[ We built this to capture some truth. ]

HOW IT WORKS

> Reciprocity Protocol (Give to Get)
It's a simple, fair contract. There's no room for silent observers in Bliip. Want to check what's happening in your area? Step out of the shadows first. Share your own fragment of the day to unlock access to the stories of others for 24 hours.

> System Directives
Every day, the System issues a challenge. It could be an order to document "urban grime," "the ugliest shoe," or "the color dominating your street." It's an excuse to get moving and look at your surroundings from a different perspective.

> Sector Radar
Forget boring maps. You observe your surroundings through a live interface. The closer you are to the center of events, the sharper the signal you receive. You see the perspective of people passing the exact same streets as you in the very same second.

> Pure Data and Zero Filters
The world is interesting enough without forcing artificial enhancements. Everything you upload vanishes permanently after 48 hours. We don't build an archive of old data. All that matters is the vibe of your city in this exact second.

> CAPTURE YOUR SECTOR'S VIBE

The System rewards engagement. Break out of passivity and build your position in the sector:

Log Streaks: Maintain consistency and document reality day by day.

Collect Colors and Trophies: Gather the unique colors of your surroundings, which unlock visual interface modifications. Your engagement physically changes the app's appearance – from colored tiles on your grid and distinctive neon stripes on notification frames, all the way to a satisfying color-coded monthly wrap-up that you can share with others.

Initialize the terminal, accept the System's challenge, and check what's really hiding around your corner.

quotes.text:
I was doom-scrolling Instagram when I asked myself: Why am I even doing this?

I'm a graphic designer, not a professional dev, but I decided to build the opposite of the "engagement at all costs" machine. No algorithm. No permanent profiles. No infinite scroll. Just GPS, reciprocity, and 48-hour ephemeral posts.

The Concept

What if posts stayed in the physical location where you took them? I built Bliip: a Vanilla JS PWA radar-based platform where content is anchored to GPS coordinates and expires after 48 hours.

I stopped calling it 'social media' and started thinking of it as a 'localized reality node' - which sounds pretentious, but bear with me. It’s not about following people; it’s about discovering the space you’re currently standing in.

Core mechanics:

Give-to-get: You must post to unlock nearby content for 24h. No lurkers allowed.
GPS-locked: Content is tied to space, not users.
The Narrator: A sarcastic "System" AI (the gatekeeper) that roasts you during onboarding.

Who is this actually for?

Bliip definitely isn't for everyone. It's for the person at a music festival, a campus, or a neighborhood block party who wants to know what the person three feet away is seeing — not what an algorithm decided they should see six hours ago.

Technical Hurdles

Schrödinger's Photo: Modern phones don't release files immediately; they process HDR/AI in the background. If you grab the file too fast, it's "not there" yet. I had to dump the Blob directly to RAM to bypass the OS …
quotes.title: I spent a year building a GPS-ephemeral social network. Here's what happened
